patients.summary: Hatfield high school math teacher who joined in 2018 with new hypertension on HCTZ; in 2020 resistant pressures with hypokalemia and high renin/aldosterone led to renal artery imaging, cardiology diagnosis of fibromuscular dysplasia, and an ED visit for transient right-eye vision loss. Losartan added in 2021 after a CTA showed multifocal right renal FMD; pressures since in the 130s-140s.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — ESTABLISH CARE

34 y/o woman, teaches math at the high school. Has not had a regular PCP for several years (prior office in another town; records release signed today). Here to get set up. Feels well.
ROS: no headaches she'd call unusual, no chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, leg swelling. Menses regular. Sleeping ok.

Intake BP 166/97. I rechecked after she sat quietly for ~10 min, both arms — still well into the 160s/90s. She does not know of any prior readings.

PMH: none
PSH: none
Meds: none
Allergies: NKDA
FH: mother has had high blood pressure since her mid-40s (dx at 45). A maternal aunt had an ischemic stroke at 52. Father — hyperlipidemia.
SH: never smoker. Wine 1-2 glasses a month. No drug use. Teaches high school mathematics.

Exam: HR 77, T 36.2, SpO2 98%. Wt 70.3 kg, ht 165.7 cm, BMI 25.6.
Pleasant, in no distress. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur or gallop. Chest clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No peripheral edema. Radial and pedal pulses 2+.

A/P
1. Hypertension, new, stage 2 range on repeated office readings. Strong maternal history. She is young for essential HTN — if it proves hard to control, will look for a secondary cause. Start hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg every morning. Salt, activity reviewed; alcohol already minimal. BMP and lipids today. Nurse BP check with BMP in about 5 weeks. Buy a validated upper-arm cuff and bring it in so we can compare.
2. Health maintenance: cervical screening due; she prefers to do it at a physical rather than today. Will check immunization history once old records arrive.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Release signed by pt. Request for complete records faxed to prior primary care office. Will scan on receipt.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Kristen — your labs from yesterday are fine. Potassium 4.1, sodium 139, kidney function normal (creatinine 0.73). Cholesterol looks good: total 180, LDL 96, HDL 64, triglycerides 99.
Start the hydrochlorothiazide tomorrow morning. You may urinate more for the first week or so. Nurse BP check in about 5 weeks — front desk will call to book.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax from pt's previous primary care office, 14 pages: office notes and annual exams 2011-2014, immunization list (no Tdap date listed). No chronic diagnoses or medications on their list. Scanned to media tab and sent to PCP inbox.
PCP review 5/10: nothing that changes current plan. No Tdap on file — offer at physical.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - BP Check
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
BP check, ~5 wks on HCTZ 25 mg daily. Takes it each morning before school, has not missed doses. Urinating more the first week, settled now. No dizziness, no cramps.
BP 161/94 R arm seated after 5 min rest, HR 87. Pt's home cuff checked against ours on the L arm — within a few points of each other.
BMP drawn. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your bloodwork on the hydrochlorothiazide is fine — potassium 4.1, sodium 139, kidney function normal. The pressure at the nurse visit (161/94) is still higher than I'd like. Give it more time with the salt and activity changes, and send me a set of home readings in a few weeks. I'd like to see you in the fall once school is back in session.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg tab, asking for 90-day supply. Last BP visit 5/24/18, labs 5/24 normal. Sent #90 with 1 refill per protocol. Pt reminded by phone to book fall BP follow-up.

documents.title: Office Visit - Hypertension
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: BP follow-up. School started; busy but ok. Takes HCTZ 25 every morning. Home log (about a dozen readings in Sept) mostly mid-140s over ~90. Walking after school 3-4 days a week. No cramps, lightheadedness or headaches.
O: BP 144/90, HR 84, wt 70.8 kg. CV: regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Ankles without edema.
A: HTN, better on thiazide but above goal (<130/80).
P: Discussed adding a second agent vs. more time on lifestyle. She'd rather work on sodium first (takeout and school cafeteria lunches are her weak spots). Agreed — recheck in the spring, sooner if home numbers climb. BMP today. Flu vaccine today.

documents.title: Home BP readings

Hi, I've been checking at home a few times a week like you asked. Most are around 145-150 on top and low 90s on the bottom, a couple in the 140s. Is that okay or should I come in before spring?
Kristen

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP f/u, rescheduled from March. Vacation week.
On HCTZ 25 daily, adherent. Home readings 140s-150s/90s. Admits the sodium changes didn't really stick over the winter. Denies headache, chest pain, SOB, visual change.
BP 157/98, HR 81, wt 70.6 kg. Heart regular, no murmur. Chest clear. Legs without swelling.

A/P: HTN not controlled on thiazide alone, a year in. I recommended adding a second agent today. She wants one more try first — a few colleagues are starting an after-school walking group — and would like to revisit at her physical in August. Accepted with a deadline: if still over 140/90 at the physical, we add a medication. BMP today.

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Cervix, liquid-based preparation.
ADEQUACY: Satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present.
INTERPRETATION: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL
35 y/o F, summer break, feels well. HTN on HCTZ 25 mg; home readings "about the same," 140s-150s/90s. The walking group lasted about a month.
ROS: negative except as above. Menses regular, no gyn concerns.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. NKDA.
FH/SH: unchanged from intake. Never smoker, rare wine.

Prevention:
- Cervical: last Pap ~2014 per old records. Co-test today.
- HIV and hepatitis C one-time screening offered — accepts.
- Tdap: none on record — given today.
- PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: BP 157/94, HR 76, T 36.7, SpO2 98%, wt 70.7 kg, BMI 25.7.
General: well. HEENT: TMs and oropharynx normal. Neck: thyroid normal size, no nodes. CV: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear. Breasts: symmetric, no masses or discharge. Abdomen: soft, no organomegaly. Pelvic: vulva and vagina unremarkable; cervix normal in appearance, cytology/HPV sample taken. Extremities: no edema. Skin: no concerning lesions.

A/P
1. Health maintenance as above. BMP today.
2. HTN, still above goal. Per our April agreement I again recommended a second agent (ACE inhibitor or amlodipine). She is reluctant to add a daily pill and asked for one more stretch with home monitoring through the fall. I documented my recommendation; she will send readings in October and we will add then if not under 140/90.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Kristen — your Pap and HPV test are both normal, so the next co-test is due in 5 years. HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Kidney function and potassium normal. The Tdap you got is good for 10 years.
Don't forget to send me home BP readings in October.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Quadrivalent flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM, L deltoid. VIS reviewed; no prior reactions. Waited 15 min in lobby without problems.
Asked about October BP readings — she has been checking but hasn't sent them; will send this weekend.

documents.title: BP question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi — I know I was supposed to send numbers in October and I never did, school got away from me. They've been creeping up. Lots of 150s and some in the 160s over 100. I feel fine otherwise. Should I come in?

documents.title: RE: BP question
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Hi Kristen, the doctor would like to see you. First after-school opening after the break is Tue 1/21 at 3:30 — booked. Please bring your cuff and log.
Note from Dr: keep taking the HCTZ. If you get readings over 180/110, a severe headache, chest pain or vision change before then, call us the same day.

events.reason: Blood pressure above goal, muscle cramps

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Resistant Hypertension
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: BP follow-up. HCTZ 25 mg daily since 4/2018, she rarely misses a dose. Home readings since November 150s-160s over 90s-100s. New: muscle cramps for a few weeks — calves and feet at night, sometimes her hands while grading. No palpitations or weakness. No licorice, decongestants, NSAIDs, energy drinks or supplements. Never smoker, rare wine. Not snoring per her report.

O: BP 166/102, same in both arms. HR 78. No edema. No bruits heard. Heart regular. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Hypertension, now behaving as resistant: never at goal on a thiazide for almost two years and rising. At 36, this needs a secondary workup. Cramps on a thiazide make me think of low potassium, which would also bring primary aldosteronism and renovascular disease into the picture.
 - BMP, plasma renin activity and aldosterone drawn today.
 - 24-hour urine metanephrines — container and instructions given.
 - Renal artery duplex ultrasound ordered. In a woman her age, fibromuscular dysplasia is the renovascular cause I'm most concerned about.
 - Cardiology referral for resistant hypertension.
 - Continue HCTZ for now so the renin/aldosterone are drawn on her usual regimen.
2. Muscle cramps — likely electrolyte; will call with BMP this afternoon.

medications.drug: potassium chloride 20 MEQ Extended Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with food

documents.title: Lab Result Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spoke with pt re: today's BMP. K 2.9, HCO3 32, Na 147 — hypokalemia with metabolic alkalosis, fits her cramps.
Start potassium chloride ER 20 mEq once daily with food. Repeat BMP in ~2 weeks; she'll come 2/3 when she drops off the 24-hr urine.
ED for palpitations, marked weakness or fainting. Renin/aldosterone are send-outs, about a week. Pt verbalized understanding.

documents.title: Renin and Aldosterone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kristen, your renin and aldosterone results are back. Both are elevated (renin activity 9.4, aldosterone 34). When both run high together, the adrenal glands are usually responding to a signal from the kidneys rather than overproducing on their own — a secondary hyperaldosteronism pattern. That fits with reduced blood flow to a kidney, which the renal artery ultrasound is designed to look for, so please keep that appointment. Still do the 24-hour urine collection and keep taking the potassium every day.

documents.title: Lab Visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt dropped off 24-hr urine collection (started Sun 2/2 AM, finished this AM), labeled and sent to reference lab. BMP drawn L antecubital, one stick. Taking KCl daily, cramps less.

documents.title: 24-Hour Urine Metanephrines
documents.author: reference lab
documents.body:
REFERENCE LABORATORY REPORT
Specimen: urine, 24-hour collection. Collected 02/02/2020-02/03/2020. Received 02/03/2020.
Test: Metanephrines, fractionated, 24-hour urine.
Metanephrine: within reference interval.
Normetanephrine: within reference interval.
Total metanephrines: within reference interval.
Interpretation: Normal. Results do not suggest pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma.

documents.title: Results Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Reached pt by phone after PCP review. 24-hr urine metanephrines normal (report scanned). BMP 2/3 on KCl: K 3.7 (up from 2.9), Na 140, HCO3 28. Continue KCl 20 mEq daily. Renal artery duplex confirmed for Wed 2/12 at 4:00, nothing to eat after lunch that day. Pt agreeable.

reports.text:
EXAM: Ultrasound, abdominal Doppler — renal arteries.
INDICATION: Resistant hypertension, hypokalemia. Elevated renin and aldosterone.
TECHNIQUE: Grayscale, color and spectral Doppler evaluation of the abdominal aorta, renal artery origins and both kidneys. Patient fasting.
FINDINGS:
Aorta: normal caliber.
Right renal artery: reduced luminal diameter with turbulent flow on color and spectral Doppler.
Left renal artery: no focal flow abnormality identified.
Kidneys: normal size and echotexture bilaterally. No hydronephrosis or mass.
reports.conclusion: Turbulent flow with reduced diameter of the right renal artery, suspicious for renal artery stenosis. Cause not determined by ultrasound; fibromuscular dysplasia is a consideration in a young woman. CTA or MRA could further characterize if clinically indicated.

documents.title: Renal Artery Ultrasound
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kristen, the ultrasound shows a narrowing of the artery to your right kidney with turbulent flow through it. In a woman your age the most common cause is fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) — a condition of the artery wall itself, not cholesterol buildup. It would explain why your pressure has been so stubborn and why the renin and aldosterone were high. Your cardiology appointment is March 11; please keep it, they will confirm the diagnosis and plan next steps. No medication changes in the meantime.

events.reason: Resistant hypertension, abnormal renal artery Doppler

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOVASCULAR MEDICINE — OUTPATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 03/11/2020
Referred by: primary care, for resistant hypertension with hypokalemia and an abnormal renal artery Doppler.

Dear Colleague,

Thank you for asking me to see Ms. Marchetti, a 36-year-old high school mathematics teacher. Hypertension was diagnosed in 2018 and has not reached goal on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. In January her potassium was 2.9 with a bicarbonate of 32, and potassium chloride 20 mEq daily was added. Plasma renin activity and aldosterone were both elevated; 24-hour urine metanephrines were normal.

When asked specifically, she describes about six months of intermittent headaches — throbbing and right-sided — sometimes accompanied by a whooshing sound in her ears that keeps time with her pulse. She had not thought to mention these before. No visual symptoms, weakness, numbness or speech difficulty. No chest pain, claudication or post-prandial abdominal pain.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; potassium chloride ER 20 mEq daily. Allergies: none known.
Family history: mother with hypertension from age 45; maternal aunt with ischemic stroke at 52; father with hyperlipidemia.
Social: never smoker; one or two glasses of wine a month.

Examination: BP 155/95 in both arms. Regular rhythm, normal S1 S2, no murmur. A high-pitched bruit is audible over the right side of the neck, and a similar high-pitched bruit in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Lungs clear. No edema. Peripheral pulses present and symmetric.

Data: Chemistry today — creatinine 0.76, potassium 4.3, both normal. Renal artery Doppler of 02/12/2020 reviewed: turbulence and reduced diameter of the right renal artery.

Impression:
1. Fibromuscular dysplasia involving the right renal artery, with renovascular hypertension. A young woman with thiazide-resistant hypertension, secondary hyperaldosteronism, an abdominal bruit and these Doppler findings — I am comfortable making this diagnosis.
2. Episodic right-sided pulsatile headache and pulsatile tinnitus.

Recommendations:
- Continue hydrochlorothiazide and potassium chloride at current doses.
- Home blood pressure log.
- Return to cardiology clinic in 3 to 4 months to review pressures and plan.

I explained that FMD is a non-atherosclerotic disease of the arterial wall. Thank you for this referral.

Cardiology

documents.title: Cardiology Letter Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cardiology consult letter (DOS 3/11) received 3/16, reviewed. Diagnosis: fibromuscular dysplasia of the right renal artery with renovascular hypertension. Their plan: continue HCTZ 25 + KCl 20, home BP log, cardiology follow-up in 3-4 months.
Called pt to go over it; questions answered. Problem list updated. She prefers a video visit for her next BP check given the pandemic — booked for May.

documents.title: Video Visit - Hypertension
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit (pt at home, consented). Teaching remotely.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily. Adherent. Cramps resolved since starting potassium.
Home cuff readings last 2 weeks, read off her log: mostly 150s/90s.
Occasional right-sided headaches, no different from what she described to cardiology. No vision changes, weakness, numbness or speech trouble.
Cardiology follow-up was planned for early summer; their office is rebooking in-person visits and she is on their list.
Exam limited to video: well appearing, speech fluent, no distress.

A/P: Renovascular HTN from right renal artery FMD, still above goal. Cardiology is directing management; continue current regimen pending their follow-up. BMP at the lab this week. Reviewed stroke warning signs — any vision loss, weakness, numbness, facial droop or speech trouble means 911.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: MA
documents.body: LM on pt's cell per PCP: BMP from today normal, potassium 4.2, creatinine 0.65. Continue current meds. Portal message sent as well.

reports.text:
EXAM: Duplex ultrasound, renal arteries.
INDICATION: Hypertension, known fibromuscular dysplasia.
FINDINGS: Renal arteries: beading and irregularity of the arterial contour. Abdominal aorta normal caliber. Kidneys normal in size, no hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion: Beading and irregularity of the renal artery, consistent with stenosis due to fibromuscular dysplasia.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN DOCUMENTATION
Date of service: 07/18/2020. Arrival 12:50. Records sent to primary care at patient request.

CHIEF COMPLAINT: Right eye vision loss, resolved.

HPI: 36-year-old woman with fibromuscular dysplasia (renal, diagnosed by her cardiologist in March) and hypertension who comes in after two episodes of losing vision in her right eye. Each lasted a few minutes and cleared completely. Painless, right eye only. She also reports severe headaches on and off since last fall, plus a "whooshing" noise in her ears; both continue. She is following with cardiology as an outpatient. No weakness, numbness, speech change or facial droop. Back to baseline now.

PMH: Hypertension, diagnosed about two years ago, poorly controlled on hydrochlorothiazide. Fibromuscular dysplasia.
PSH: None.
MEDICATIONS: Hydrochlorothiazide; potassium chloride.
ALLERGIES: NKDA.
FAMILY HISTORY: Noncontributory.
SOCIAL: Never smoker. Wine 1-2 glasses per month. High school math teacher.

VITALS: BP 162/98 right arm, 154/92 left arm. HR 82, RR 16, T 36.7 C, SpO2 99% room air.

EXAM:
General: alert, comfortable.
Eyes: pupils equal and reactive, no afferent defect. Visual fields full to confrontation. Acuity grossly intact each eye.
Neck: supple. No carotid bruits.
CV: regular rate and rhythm.
Lungs: clear.
Abdomen: soft, nontender. High-pitched epigastric bruit.
Neuro: cranial nerves II-XII intact. Strength 5/5 all extremities. Sensation intact. Finger-to-nose and gait normal.

RESULTS: BMP — renal function normal (BUN 14, creatinine 0.71), potassium 4.2.
Renal artery duplex: beading and irregularity consistent with stenosis from fibromuscular dysplasia (see report).

ED COURSE / MDM: Two brief episodes of right monocular vision loss, fully resolved, with a normal neurological examination. Renal function normal. Duplex consistent with her known FMD. Blood pressure elevated without symptoms of end-organ injury here. She is at baseline and has primary care and cardiology follow-up in place.

DIAGNOSES: Transient vision loss, right eye. Fibromuscular dysplasia. Hypertension.

DISPOSITION: Discharged home in stable condition. Follow up with primary care within one week and with cardiology. Return immediately for recurrent vision loss, weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, or a sudden severe headache.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: ER visit Saturday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know I went to the ER on Saturday. I lost the vision in my right eye twice, for a few minutes each time. It came back completely. They said my neuro exam was normal and to follow up with you and cardiology. I'm fine now, just a little shaken. Can I get in this week or next?

documents.title: RE: ER visit Saturday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're okay, and thank you for letting me know. We've requested the ER records. Front desk has you for Tue 7/28 at 10:30. If the vision loss happens again — even briefly — call 911 rather than waiting it out.

documents.title: Office Visit - ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED FOLLOW-UP
Seen 7/18 in an outside ED for two brief episodes of right monocular vision loss, minutes each, full recovery. ED records reviewed: normal neuro exam, epigastric bruit, normal renal function, renal duplex with beading/irregularity c/w FMD. Discharged to outpatient follow-up.
Since then: no further episodes. Headaches a bit less often this month; the whooshing comes and goes. Taking HCTZ 25 and KCl 20 daily. Home BP still 150s/90s.
Cardiology: the 3-4 month follow-up has not happened; their office is still working through postponed visits. She will call them this week and we will fax the ED records over.

Exam: BP 150/99, HR 80, wt 70.8 kg. Alert, fluent speech. Pupils equal, EOM full, fields full to confrontation. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Strength symmetric, gait normal.

A/P
1. Transient right monocular vision loss, resolved, in a patient with FMD and uncontrolled BP. ED evaluation reassuring; no new deficits. 911 precautions reviewed again.
2. Renovascular HTN / right renal artery FMD, above goal. Continue HCTZ 25 and KCl 20 for now; cardiology to direct further management. BMP today. ED records to cardiology.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requests 90-day supplies: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and potassium chloride ER 20 mEq. Last visit 7/28/20, BMP 7/28 normal. Sent both, #90 x1 refill, per PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL
37 y/o F. Back teaching in person. Feels well. No further vision episodes since July. Occasional headaches. Home BP 140s-150s/90s.
Cardiology: still no follow-up date. Their office told her they would call; gave her the scheduling line again.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; potassium chloride ER 20 mEq daily. NKDA.

Prevention: Pap/HPV 8/2019 normal. Tdap 2019. HIV/HCV screened 2019. Flu vaccine today. PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: BP 138/88, HR 78, T 36.7, SpO2 97%, wt 69.8 kg, BMI 25.4.
Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin clear.

A/P
1. Renovascular HTN / FMD: today's office reading is the best she has had, but her home log is still above goal. No change today; BMP. Pushing cardiology follow-up — she will call them, we'll send a referral reminder.
2. Health maintenance up to date; flu given.

documents.title: BP log
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Here are my numbers since Thanksgiving, mostly mornings before school: 150-158 over 94-100. Still haven't heard from cardiology.

documents.title: RE: BP log
documents.author: RN

documents.title: Office Visit - Hypertension
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
HTN FOLLOW-UP (seen 3/16; labs back this morning)
Routine follow-up of severe hypertension with right renal artery FMD (dx cardiology 3/2020), with prior transient right-eye vision loss (7/2020), headaches and pulsatile tinnitus. Today she denies headache, vision changes or chest pain. Home readings have run higher this winter. Cardiology follow-up never got rebooked.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily.

BP 180/120 (repeated after rest, similar), HR 76.
Exam normal: alert, comfortable; heart regular, no murmur; lungs clear; abdomen soft; no edema; neuro nonfocal.
Labs 3/16: creatinine and electrolytes normal — Cr 0.66, K 4.0, Na 140, HCO3 28.

A/P
1. Renovascular HTN due to right renal artery FMD — severely elevated, asymptomatic, no sign of acute end-organ injury. Add losartan 25 mg daily (unilateral disease, normal renal function). Continue HCTZ 25. Continue KCl for now; BMP in 1-2 weeks given ARB.
2. CT angiogram of the abdomen ordered to define the renal artery disease.
3. Pregnancy: losartan can harm a developing pregnancy. Counselled; she reports reliable contraception and no plans for pregnancy. Stop it and call right away if pregnancy is ever possible.
4. Will send CTA result to cardiology with another request for follow-up.
ED for severe headache, vision loss, chest pain or neuro symptoms. Recheck 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your bloodwork two weeks into losartan looks good — creatinine 0.73 (0.66 before) and potassium 4.5. Your kidneys are tolerating it. CT angiogram is booked for 4/8.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
EXAM: CT angiography of the abdomen.
INDICATION: Renovascular hypertension; known fibromuscular dysplasia of the right renal artery on ultrasound; anatomic evaluation.
TECHNIQUE: Arterial-phase helical CT of the abdomen after intravenous contrast, with multiplanar and 3D reformations.
FINDINGS:
Abdominal aorta: normal caliber.
Right renal artery: single artery with an irregular, beaded appearance and a focal area of narrowing. No aneurysm or dissection identified.
Left renal artery: single artery, normal in caliber and contour.
Kidneys: normal in size bilaterally with symmetric enhancement. No hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion:
1. Beaded, irregular right renal artery with focal narrowing, consistent with multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia.
2. Normal left renal artery.
3. Kidneys normal in size.

documents.title: CT Angiogram Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kristen, the CT angiogram confirms fibromuscular dysplasia in the artery to your right kidney — the beaded pattern typical of the multifocal type, with one narrowed area. The artery to your left kidney is normal and both kidneys are a normal size. I'm sending the report to cardiology. Keep logging your pressures; next BP visit in early June.
